stages.name: Persian-held
stages.desc: Ruled by the Great King's satraps and garrisons

stages.name: Phoenician & Cypriot fleet cities
stages.desc: City-kingdoms whose warships serve the Persian fleet

stages.name: Contested by the Persian fleet
stages.desc: Islands and coasts raided, retaken or blockaded from the sea

stages.name: Macedonian & allied
stages.desc: Macedon, its Thracian subjects and the Greek League of Corinth

stages.name: Gone over to Alexander
stages.desc: Surrendered to or conquered by Alexander

stages.name: Hostile or neutral Greeks
stages.desc: Greek states outside the League or in arms against Macedon

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Salamis, Kition, Amathus, Kourion and the other city-kingdoms man ships for Persia
After Issus the Cypriot kings bring about 120 ships to Sidon and join Alexander

states.name: Israel
timeline: Persian province of the coast and hills; Phoenician-run ports such as Akko and Dor
The coast submits as Alexander marches from Tyre to Gaza

states.name: Palestine
timeline: Gaza, the Persian fortress-city on the road to Egypt
Gaza falls after a two-month siege; its men are killed, women and children enslaved

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Tyre, Sidon and Byblos: the heart of the Great King's navy
Byblos opens its gates as Alexander marches south; Sidon follows that winter, Tyre refuses him
Tyre falls after a seven-month siege; its people are killed or enslaved

states.name: Syria
timeline: Persian Syria; the island-city of Arwad (Aradus) sends its king and ships to the fleet
Damascus and Darius's baggage are taken; Arwad's prince crowns Alexander with gold

states.name: North Macedonia
timeline: Paeonia and the Upper Macedonian cantons, ruled from Pella since Philip II
Alexander marches north through Paeonia against the Triballi and the Illyrians

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Western Anatolia under Persian satraps; a Macedonian advance force lands near Abydos
Memnon drives Parmenion's advance force back to the Hellespont
After the Granicus, Sardis, Ephesus, Miletus and Halicarnassus fall to Alexander
The Persian fleet retakes Tenedos and still holds Halicarnassus's citadels
Antigonus beats the Persian survivors of Issus; the last coastal strongholds fall

states.name: Greece
timeline: Macedon and the League of Corinth, sworn to Philip's war on Persia; Sparta alone stays out
Thebes revolts and is razed; the rest of Greece submits to Alexander
Memnon takes Chios and Lesbos; Persian squadrons reach the Cyclades and Siphnos
Hegelochus and Amphoterus retake Chios, Lesbos and Cos; the Aegean is Macedonian again
Agis III of Sparta leads the Peloponnese in war against Macedon

states.name: Bulgaria
timeline: Thracian tribes made tributary by Philip; restless at the news of his murder
Alexander crushes the Triballi and crosses the Danube against the Getae
Memnon, Macedon's governor in Thrace (no kin of the Rhodian), revolts and draws Antipater north

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Reconquered by Persia in 343 BC after six decades of independence
The satrap Mazaces surrenders Egypt to Alexander without a fight
Alexander founds Alexandria and visits the oracle of Ammon at Siwa

events.title: Philip murdered
events.text: Philip II is stabbed by a bodyguard in the theatre at Aegae; his twenty-year-old son Alexander becomes king.

events.title: Advance force lands
events.text: Parmenion and Attalus cross into Asia with about ten thousand men to prepare the invasion.

events.title: Memnon at Cyzicus
events.text: The Rhodian mercenary general Memnon tries to seize Cyzicus by surprise for Persia.

events.title: Parmenion checked
events.text: Memnon defeats Parmenion near Magnesia and pens the Macedonians into a bridgehead on the Hellespont.

events.title: Thebes razed
events.text: Alexander storms rebellious Thebes; six thousand are killed and the survivors sold into slavery.

events.title: Against the Triballi
events.text: Alexander campaigns in Thrace and crosses the Danube to secure Macedon's northern frontier.

events.title: Persian gold refused
events.text: Darius offers Athens three hundred talents; the assembly officially refuses the money.

events.title: Hellespont crossing
events.text: Alexander crosses to Asia with about thirty-seven thousand men, ferried by 160 warships.

events.title: Battle of the Granicus
events.text: The satraps reject Memnon's advice to burn the land and are routed; the Greek mercenaries in Persian service are massacred.

events.title: Sardis surrenders
events.text: The Lydian capital and its treasury are handed over without a fight.

events.title: Race to Lade
events.text: Nicanor's 160 Greek ships reach Lade three days before a Persian fleet of about four hundred.

events.title: Miletus stormed
events.text: Alexander takes Miletus while the Persian fleet, cut off from water, lies helpless at Mycale.

events.title: Fleet disbanded
events.text: Short of money and outmatched at sea, Alexander sends his fleet home, keeping only a few ships, among them twenty from Athens.

events.title: Siege of Halicarnassus
events.text: Memnon defends the Carian capital for weeks, then burns it and withdraws to its citadels and to Cos.

events.title: Memnon in command
events.text: Darius makes Memnon commander of the whole coast and fleet; his wife and children go to the court as pledges.

events.title: Chios betrayed
events.text: Memnon's fleet takes Chios with the help of an oligarchic faction inside the city.

events.title: Lesbos goes over
events.text: Antissa, Methymna, Pyrrha and Eresos join the Persians without a fight.

events.title: Siege of Mytilene
events.text: Memnon walls Mytilene off with a double stockade and five camps; his ships watch from Cape Sigri.

events.title: Memnon dies
events.text: Memnon falls ill and dies before Mytilene, leaving his command to his nephew Pharnabazus.

events.title: Mytilene surrenders
events.text: The city yields on terms; the Persians install a Rhodian garrison and a tyrant, Diogenes.

events.title: Gordian knot
events.text: Inland, Alexander cuts or loosens the knot at Gordium while his rear is threatened from the sea.

events.title: Tenedos submits
events.text: Pharnabazus and Autophradates bring a hundred ships to Tenedos, at the mouth of the Hellespont.

events.title: Ambush off Siphnos
events.text: Proteas sails from Chalcis with fifteen ships and captures eight of Datames's ten.

events.title: Battle of Issus
events.text: Darius is defeated and flees, leaving his mother, wife and children in Alexander's hands.

events.title: Agis at Siphnos
events.text: Agis III of Sparta meets the Persian admirals; as news of Issus arrives, he leaves with thirty talents and ten triremes.

events.title: Damascus taken
events.text: Parmenion seizes the Persian court's treasure and the Greek envoys waiting there.

events.title: Arwad submits
events.text: Straton, son of King Gerostratus, meets Alexander and crowns him with a golden wreath.

events.title: Byblos yields
events.text: King Enylus's city opens its gates while he serves with the Persian fleet.

events.title: Ships burned at Tripoli
events.text: Fleeing Issus, the renegade Amyntas burns the surplus Persian ships beached at Tripolis.

events.title: Sidon welcomes Alexander
events.text: Sidon opens its gates; Alexander deposes King Straton and installs Abdalonymus.

events.title: The fleet changes sides
events.text: About eighty Phoenician ships desert Autophradates; 120 Cypriot ships follow them to Sidon.

events.title: Siege of Tyre
events.text: Alexander builds a mole to the island city and assaults it with the Phoenician and Cypriot fleets.

events.title: Tyre falls
events.text: After seven months, about eight thousand Tyrians are killed and thirty thousand sold into slavery.

events.title: Agis in Crete
events.text: With Persian ships and money, the Spartans win over most of the Cretan cities.

events.title: Pharnabazus captured
events.text: Hegelochus retakes Chios; Pharnabazus is taken prisoner but later escapes his guards at Cos.

events.title: Mytilene retaken
events.text: The Athenian Chares gives up Mytilene with two thousand men; the Lesbian cities return.

events.title: Siege of Gaza
events.text: Gaza holds out for two months; its men are killed and its women and children enslaved.

events.title: Antigonus in Anatolia
events.text: Alexander's satrap of Phrygia defeats Persian survivors of Issus trying to retake Asia Minor.

events.title: Egypt surrenders
events.text: The satrap Mazaces hands over Memphis and Egypt without a fight.

events.title: Alexandria founded
events.text: Alexander lays out a new city on the coast west of the Nile's Canopic mouth.

events.title: Oracle at Siwa
events.text: Alexander crosses the desert to consult the oracle of Ammon.

events.title: Fleet to the Peloponnese
events.text: Back at Tyre, Alexander sends Amphoterus with a fleet to support Greeks against Sparta.

events.title: Agis goes to war
events.text: Sparta and its allies raise some twenty thousand foot; Athens stays out.

events.title: Megalopolis besieged
events.text: Agis besieges the pro-Macedonian city, where Antipater's larger army will destroy him.

chartNote: Share of the area of ten present-day countries, coloured by the allegiance of the part that mattered in the war at sea. Regions are today's boundaries; ancient satrapies, city-kingdoms and islands did not follow them, and a single island could change sides within weeks. A simplification; Egypt's desert weighs heavily in the shares.
